title: Open-plan office noise: Cognitive performance and restoration

findings.mechanism: Noise impairs working memory processes involved in recalling words.
findings.quote: a significant main effect of noise on memory for words (PI-points), F (1, 30) = 4.27, p < .05, partial ŋ² = 0.13, indicating a better performance in low noise compared with high noise

findings.mechanism: Noise leads to more forgotten words, indicating impaired memory retrieval.
findings.quote: a significant effect of noise on the number of missing answers (PI-no answers), F (1, 30) = 6.62, p < .05, partial ŋ² = 0.18.

findings.consequent: other cognitive measures (Flanker, Logical problems, Operation span, Reading span, Serial recall, Shifting, Updating)
findings.mechanism: The specific noise conditions did not affect these cognitive functions, possibly due to task independence or compensation.
findings.quote: There were, however, no statistically significant effects of noise on the other cognitive measures (all Fs < 1).

findings.mechanism: Decline in cortisol levels is consistent with normal circadian variation.
findings.quote: a significant effect of time on the cortisol levels F (1.16, 34.91) = 31.12, p < .001, partial ŋ² = 0.51

findings.mechanism: Short-term noise exposure did not significantly affect the decline in cortisol levels.
findings.quote: There was no statistically significant effect of noise on the decline in the level of cortisol (F < 1).

findings.mechanism: Decline in norepinephrine levels is consistent with normal physiological patterns over time.
findings.quote: A significant effect of time was also shown on the norepinephrine levels from the urine samples, F (1, 35) = 30.40, p < 0.001, partial ŋ² = 0.47

findings.mechanism: Short-term noise exposure did not significantly affect catecholamine levels.
findings.quote: There were no statistically significant effects of noise on the level of catecholamines (F < 1).

findings.mechanism: Working in high noise for 2 hours leads to increased self-reported tiredness.
findings.quote: a significant interaction between noise and time on tiredness (yawning), F (2, 32) = 6.25, p < 0.01, partial ŋ² = 0.28

findings.mechanism: Working in high noise for 2 hours leads to increased self-reported lack of motivation.
findings.quote: and on lack of motivation (passiveness) F (2, 32) = 4.33, p < 0.05, partial ŋ² = 0.21.

findings.antecedent: restorative conditions (nature movie with sound, river sound only, silence, office noise)
findings.consequent: change in self-rated lack of energy (exhaustion)
findings.mechanism: Different restorative conditions lead to varying degrees of energy restoration.
findings.quote: a significant between-subjects effect of restorative conditions on change in the ratings of lack of energy (exhaustion), F (3, 29) = 3.10, p < 0.05, partial ŋ² = 0.24

findings.antecedent: nature movie with sound during restoration
findings.mechanism: Multi-sensory nature stimuli (visual and auditory) are more restorative for energy than office noise.
findings.quote: participants who saw the movie (including river sounds) rated themselves as having more energy (i.e., were less exhausted) in comparison with the participants listening to noise (p < 0.01)

findings.antecedent: nature movie with sound during restoration
findings.mechanism: Multi-sensory nature stimuli (visual and auditory) are more restorative for energy than auditory-only nature sounds.
findings.quote: and those listening to river sounds (p < 0.05).

findings.antecedent: restorative conditions (nature movie with sound, river sound only, silence, office noise)
findings.consequent: change in self-rated lack of motivation (uninterested)
findings.mechanism: Different restorative conditions lead to varying degrees of motivation restoration.
findings.quote: and of lack of motivation (uninterested) F (3, 29) = 3.02, p < 0.05, partial ŋ² = 0.24.

findings.mechanism: Remaining in office noise during restoration negatively impacts motivation compared to listening to river sounds.
findings.quote: participants who listened to noise during the restoration period rated themselves as being less motivated (i.e., more uninterested) in comparison with the participants who listened to river sounds (p < 0.05)

findings.mechanism: Remaining in office noise during restoration negatively impacts motivation compared to watching a nature movie.

findings.antecedent: nature movie with sound during restoration
findings.mechanism: Nature movie with sound marginally reduces tiredness compared to office noise.
findings.quote: a marginal difference in tiredness (yawning) between the movie condition and the noise condition (p = 0.055)

findings.antecedent: nature movie with sound during restoration
findings.mechanism: Nature movie with sound marginally reduces tiredness compared to river sounds only.
findings.quote: and between the movie and river sound conditions (p = 0.052).

findings.antecedent: restoration period (7 min) with varying sound conditions
findings.mechanism: The short restoration period or small sample size may have prevented detection of effects on objective measures.
findings.quote: No statistically significant effects from the restoration period were detected on the cognitive or physiological measures.

stimuli.description: Simulated open-plan office with 8 workstations, 1.43m high screens, windows to a white room with simulated outdoor lighting.
High noise (51 LAeq) from actual open-plan office recordings with added phone and speech signals (conversations from radio).
Low noise (39 LAeq) from actual open-plan office recordings with added phone and speech signals, reduced by 12 dB compared to high noise.
Nature movie clips of streaming water (rivers) with corresponding river sounds.
River sounds only (binaural recording of shallow, slow river with birds chirping).
Office noise (continued from work period) during restoration.

tables.description: Analysis of two noise conditions (high noise: 51 dBA, low noise: 39 dBA) in respect to Speech Transmission Index (STI) and time variation.
Mean change in SOFI-measures (Sleepy, Exhaustion, Passive, Yawning, Worn out, Uninterested) in different restorative conditions (Movie, River, Silence, Noise) from before to after the rest period.

limitations: Some cognitive measures interacted with the sequence of noise conditions, leading to a between-subjects analysis for the first session only.
Small sample size for comparison in each restorative condition.
Brief period allowed for restoration (7 minutes).
Confounding between tests and time on task for cognitive measures (addressed by fixed order and filler tasks).
Exposure times (2 hours) might be too short for performance effects to appear, as compensation for adverse sound conditions might occur.
Participants' knowledge of session duration might have mitigated tolerance to noise exposure.
The study did not find reliable noise effects on physiological measures, suggesting short-term exposure might not mediate cognitive performance effects via physiology.
